findings.title: Cache key uses Python's `hash()` which is non-deterministic across processes
findings.body: The cache key is constructed using `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`. Python's built-in `hash()` is randomized per-process (via PYTHONHASHSEED) since Python 3.3. In a multi-worker deployment, each worker will compute a different hash for the same tuple of project IDs, producing different cache keys. This means the cache is never shared between workers, completely defeating the caching purpose and causing every request to hit the allowlist lookup. Additionally, `invalidate_upsampling_cache` on line 73 uses the same `hash()` call, so it would also fail to find the correct key from a different process.

findings.title: Accidental git submodule committed at repository root
findings.body: A git submodule reference (`Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a`) has been added as a file named `sentry-repo` at the repository root. This appears to be an accidental commit (likely from running a command inside a nested clone). It will cause `git clone` to fail or produce warnings for anyone cloning the repository, and pollutes the repo structure.

findings.title: Upsampling check uses outer `dataset` variable instead of `scoped_dataset` parameter
findings.body: Inside `_get_event_stats`, the call to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` uses the `dataset` variable from the outer `get()` method's scope, not the `scoped_dataset` parameter that `_get_event_stats` actually queries against. In the dashboard widget split logic (lines 362-380), `_get_event_stats` is called with `split_dataset = discover` while the outer `dataset` may be different. This means the upsampling eligibility check evaluates the wrong dataset, potentially applying upsampling transforms to a non-errors query or failing to apply them when the split dataset is errors.

findings.title: Substring check for `event.type:error` matches negated queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` uses a simple substring check `'event.type:error' in query`. This will incorrectly match negated queries like `!event.type:error` or `NOT event.type:error`, causing upsampling to be applied when the user is explicitly excluding error events. This would produce incorrect (upsampled) counts for non-error data.

findings.title: Transformed column `upsampled_count() as count` embeds an alias that may not be parsed correctly by all query paths
findings.body: The transformation produces the string `"upsampled_count() as count"` which embeds an alias. This string is passed to `timeseries_columns`, `y_axes`, and `selected_columns` parameters across different query execution paths (RPC, top events, standard). These parameters typically expect bare function expressions without embedded aliases. If the downstream query builder doesn't parse the `as count` suffix correctly, it will either fail or produce a column with an unexpected name, breaking result processing.

findings.title: Falsy check on `client_sample_rate` silently drops a sample rate of 0
findings.body: The condition `if client_sample_rate:` on line 349 will be falsy when `client_sample_rate` is `0` or `0.0`. While a zero sample rate may be unusual, the function silently ignores it rather than raising or logging, which could mask configuration errors. More importantly, the function sets `normalized_data['sample_rate']` but the Snuba query uses `Column('sample_weight')` — if `sample_weight` is expected to be `1/sample_rate`, there's a missing transformation step, and the test expectation of count=10 (from rate 0.1) would only work if something else computes `sample_weight = 1/0.1 = 10`.

findings.title: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never called anywhere
findings.body: The function `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is provided for cache invalidation when the allowlist changes, but no code in this PR (or presumably elsewhere) ever calls it. Combined with the broken `hash()`-based cache key, this means there is no mechanism to invalidate stale cache entries when the project allowlist is updated, leading to up to 60 seconds of serving incorrect upsampling decisions after configuration changes.

findings.title: `upsampled_count` uses `sum(sample_weight)` without handling NULL values
findings.body: The `upsampled_count` function computes `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. If any event in an allowlisted project has a NULL `sample_weight` (e.g., events ingested before the feature was enabled, or events missing the error_sampling context), ClickHouse's `sum()` will skip NULLs, producing an undercount. The code comment claims the schema guarantees `sample_weight` exists, but historical data or edge cases may violate this assumption, silently producing incorrect counts.
